findings.summary: Wrong-account recovery reused a global browser idempotency key and conflicted on the correct-account retry.
A valid late resend and acceptance caused O-202 reconciliation to throw UNRECONCILED_AUDIT.
Trusted invitation and idempotency records failed open for exact temporal, path-identity, workspace, and operation invariants.
The sealed manifest omitted the direct O-202 consumer packages/hosted/src/outcome-report.ts.

remediation: Scope the browser acceptance key by invitation and authenticated UID, clear mismatch state, and bind server acceptance idempotency to the link digest and identity.
Associate each acceptance with the latest applicable resend window while preserving the first-invitation O-202 cohort and verifying every invitation audit.
Fail closed on exact seven-day temporal ordering, lifecycle revision/send-count, invitation-token linkage, and idempotency path/operation/outcome invariants.
Expand the sealed boundary to include packages/hosted/src/outcome-report.ts and the historical Review 1 request.

review_questions: Do all four Review 1 counterexamples fail to reproduce, including wrong-account/new-link acceptance recovery, valid late resend reconciliation, coordinated expiry extension, and foreign id/workspace idempotency replay without raw-token leakage?
Are terminal, revoke, resend, already-active, removed-member reactivation, concurrency, and replay transitions exact, atomic, bounded, and retry-safe under both valid and tampered ledgers?

Do list/create/resend/revoke require an active exact-workspace owner across web, REST, MCP, and personal-token principals, with pending/member/removed/foreign callers denied through CT-135 authorization?
Can any raw invitation secret appear in Firestore, audit/event/idempotency data, logs, request URLs, HTML, or owner list responses outside the one-time response and browser fragment/POST body?
Does wrong-email Google acceptance remain enumeration-safe and non-consuming while every terminal or malformed secret returns the documented safe outcome?

Do pending invitations remain outside active seat quantity, and do O-202/G-202 preserve the first-invite cohort while associating acceptance with the latest applicable resend and reconciling every audit?
Do Firestore rules keep invitation, token, idempotency, product-event, and mutation-audit collections client-private while preserving valid CT-135 membership behavior?
Does the UI preserve required owner and invitee facts, keyboard-complete controls, exact-account recovery, terminal recovery, and fragment-only link handling?
Is the expanded 47-file manifest complete for every direct invitation, membership, measurement, configuration, test, and evidence consumer, with excluded scope still absent?

findings.summary: Acceptance sampled trusted time before the transaction, allowing a regressed or retry-stale timestamp to activate a seat while persisting acceptedAt before lastSentAt.
A superseded token record lacked a server-authenticated immutable binding, so re-linking it to another invitation/workspace disclosed foreign preview facts.

decision_contract.pass: Every manifest hash and required check passes, all four prior counterexamples are closed, no actionable P0-P3 finding remains, and the reviewer returns explicit PASS with Done eligibility limited to implementation output.
decision_contract.fail: Any actionable P0-P3 correctness, security, privacy, accessibility, evidence, manifest-completeness, or scope finding returns explicit FAIL; CT-136 remains In Progress and must be remediated and resealed.
